paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about. Hezekiah tried to buy peace with silver and with the gold off the temple doors, and the Assyrians came anyway (2 Kings 18:14-17). Sometimes you do everything you can to make the trouble go away, and it just keeps on coming. I know that feeling, friend. I've paid for peace with everything I had and still ended up in the back of a drawer.

Now listen to the Rabshakeh, the Assyrian officer doing all the shouting. He asks, "What is the basis of this confidence of yours?" (2 Kings 18:19). He lists reasons to doubt, says the LORD sent him (2 Kings 18:25), and warns the men on the wall about what's coming for them (2 Kings 18:27). Then he tells them not to let Hezekiah persuade them to trust in the LORD (2 Kings 18:30) and promises a nice life if they'll make peace with him (2 Kings 18:31-32). Threats and sweet promises, and all of it pointed at the Assyrian army and away from the LORD.

So what do you do when the loud voice is shouting from the wall? The people "remained silent and did not answer a word" (2 Kings 18:36), because Hezekiah had commanded them not to answer him. They didn't have to win the argument, they just didn't take the bait. The officials came back to Hezekiah with their clothes torn (2 Kings 18:37), and this story isn't over, friend.
